Which feature is shared by all mammals?
Females have mammary glands that produce milk
The body is covered in scales
Female mammals have mammary glands which produce milk for the young to suckle.
How many chambers does a mammal's heart have?
The manual states that the mammal heart is 4 chambered.
How many specialised hearing bones are found in the inner ear of a mammal?
The inner ear of a mammal has a system of 3 highly specialised bones for hearing.
Mammals are described as endothermic. What does this mean?
Mammals are endothermic (warm-blooded) and have hair at some stage of development.
In the manual's taxonomic example, to which family does the African wild dog belong?
The taxonomic breakdown of the wild dog lists Order Carnivora, Family Canidae.
What is the scientific name (genus and species) of the African wild dog?
The manual's taxonomic example gives the wild dog's genus and species as Lycaon pictus.
What is oestrus in female mammals?
The stage when oestrogen peaks before ovulation
The stage when the young are weaned
The period when milk is produced
The time the egg is fertilised
Oestrus is the stage when the oestrogen (female hormone) level peaks before ovulation.
When the egg is released, ready to be fertilised
When the male tests the female's scent
Ovulation is when the egg is released, ready to be fertilised.
The word 'flehmen' comes from German. What does it mean?
Flehmen comes from the German word meaning "exposing teeth".
What is another name for the vomeronasal organ?
The vomeronasal organ (Jacobson's organ) is an extra smell sense designed to interpret pheromones.
In which two species does the manual say females have synchronised oestrus?
Synchronised oestrus takes place in cooperative breeders such as wild dog and hyaena.
What is the benefit of synchronised oestrus to the alpha female?
Less time spent guarding against other females mating
Her young are born in the dry season
She can mate with more males
It reduces the time alpha females spend guarding against other females mating and producing unwanted young.
The female only ovulates through sustained mating
The female ovulates once a year
The male controls when the female is in oestrus
The female ovulates only after giving birth
With induced ovulation the female only ovulates through sustained sexual intercourse, often 3-5 days after mating begins.
In which group of animals does the manual say induced ovulation occurs?
Induced ovulation occurs, inter alia, amongst elephant, lion and leopard.
What is the process of producing milk for newborn mammals called?
Newborn mammals depend on milk which is produced in a process called lactation.
According to the manual's table, what is the average weight of a male elephant?
The table gives male elephant weight as 5500-6000kg (females 3800-4000kg).
According to the table, which of these animals has females that are heavier than males?
The table gives spotted hyaena males as 62kg and females as 68kg.
According to the table, what is the average shoulder height of a male lion?
The table lists the male lion at 190kg and 1m shoulder height.
About how much food does a bull elephant need each day?
Bulls need about 170kg of food a day and only digest about 40% of it.
Approximately how much water does a bull elephant drink per day?
Bulls drink approximately 160 litres of water per day.
Why are elephants active both by day and at night?
They feed for up to 18 hours a day
They avoid lions during the day
Bulls search for females at night
Because of the large amount of food needed, elephant feed for up to 18 hours a day.
An elephant that is alert to a threat may stop, listen and raise its trunk. What else may it do while identifying the disturbance?
Alert elephant may "mock-feed" while trying to identify the disturbance.
What does a serious elephant charge usually look like?
Head down, ears back, little noise, maximum speed
Head high, ears spread, loud trumpeting
Head shaking with loud ear flaps
Walking backwards with the tail held sideways
A serious charge is usually head down, ears back, minimum noise and maximum speed.
An elephant runs at you with head held high, ears spread and trumpeting. What must a guide remember?
It can turn into a serious charge with no warning
It will never follow through with the charge
It means the elephant is in musth
Although it may be a mock-charge, the elephant can change its mind in a split second and charge seriously.
You are on foot and a bull elephant has detected you. You cannot reach cover. What should you do?
If detected by a bull and you cannot get to safety, stand your ground and tell guests to stay calm.
If a bull elephant approaches a guide standing his ground, what does the manual advise?
Hold arms up and out and step towards it
Turn your back and walk away slowly
Hold your arms up and out to look bigger and take a step towards the elephant.
Why is standing your ground less effective with a breeding herd?
Cows with calves are not easily bluffed
The manual states that cows with calves are not as easily bluffed by standing your ground.
How does a submissive elephant behave?
Keeps its head down and does not face the other elephant
Faces the other elephant with ears spread
Trumpets loudly and shakes its head
A submissive elephant keeps its head down and will not face the other elephant head on.
What is the gestation period of an elephant?
Elephant are born after a gestation of 22 months, mostly in the rainy season.
What is musth in bull elephants?
A state of raised testosterone, aggression and sexual desire
The time when young bulls leave the herd
A skin disease of older bulls
The period when cows give birth
Musth is a state of elevated testosterone causing more aggression and sexual desire.
From what age do bull elephants come into full-blown musth lasting several months?
Musth is weak from about 20-25 up to 35; after 35, bulls come into full-blown musth.
At what age do young bull elephants usually leave the breeding herd?
Young bulls leave between 12-15 years of age and join other bulls.
Who makes up an elephant family unit?
One dominant bull and his cows
Young bulls of the same age
Breeding herds are made up of family units of grandmothers, their daughters and granddaughters.
Many elephant calls are in 'infra-sound'. What does this mean?
The sound is too low for humans to hear
The sound is made only underwater
The sound is made through the trunk
Infra-sound is below the frequency that humans can hear.
Which feature helps to identify a black rhino?
A large nuchal hump on the neck
Calves that run in front of the mother
Black rhino are smaller, hold a smaller head high, have a prehensile lip and no large nuchal hump.
How do black rhino calves run in relation to their mothers?
Black rhino calves run behind their mothers, while white rhino calves run in front.
Black rhino are seldom more than how far from water?
Black rhino are water-dependent and seldom more than 15km from water.
What is the best sense of a rhino?
Rhino may run into the down-wind position to use their best sense - smell.
If a black rhino charge comes your way on foot, what does the manual advise?
Clap and shout to try to break the charge
Lie down flat on the ground
Try to get behind cover or up high; if the charge comes your way, clap and shout at the rhino.
Why should you stay off paths when black rhino are around?
Some charges are misdirected attempts to escape
Black rhino may charge repeatedly; some charges are misdirected escapes, so stay off paths.
What is the gestation period of a black rhino?
Black rhino are born after a gestation period of 15 months.
What are black rhino 'middens' actually used for?
Shared latrines that show who is in the area
Feeding sites shared by the group
Middens are shared latrines that tell other rhino who is around and advertise breeding condition.
At what time of day does most white rhino drinking take place?
Most white rhino drinking is between 17h00 and 21h00.
What is the gestation period of a white rhino?
White rhino are born after a gestation of 16 months.
How do white rhino bulls mark territory?
White rhino bulls mark territory with dung middens and urine spraying; cows are not territorial.
Why are white rhino calves seldom preyed upon by hyaena?
They are protected by the other rhino in the group
Unlike black rhino, white rhino calves are protected by the rest of the rhino in the group.
How much grass does a hippo graze each night?
Hippo feed mainly at night and graze about 40kg of grass every night.
Which statement about hippo digestion is correct?
They are the only large non-ruminant foregut fermenters
They are hindgut fermenters like zebra
They are ruminants that chew the cud
They have a simple acid stomach
Hippo are the only large non-ruminant foregut fermenters found in Botswana.
Which hippo behaviours are serious warning signs, often followed by a charge?
Taking a few steps towards you and opening the mouth
Taking a few steps towards you and opening the mouth are serious warning signs.
A hippo charges while you are moving guests away on foot. What should you do?
Get to cover fast and keep clear of its path to water
Move between the hippo and the water
There is no point standing your ground; get to cover and never block its path to the water.
According to the manual, up to how many people are killed by hippo in Africa each year?
Hippo kill more people than any other wild mammal, with up to 2900 killed each year in Africa.
What is the gestation period of a hippo?
Hippo calves are born after a very short gestation of only 8 months.
About what percentage of hippo bulls will ever hold a territory?
Only about 10% of hippo bulls will ever hold territory.
What is the major predator of buffalo?
The major predator of buffalo is lion; hyaena occasionally kill them and crocodiles take young.
A serious buffalo charge often begins with which sound?
Often the serious charge begins with a guttural growl.
A buffalo begins a serious charge towards you and your guests. What does the manual advise?
Do not stand your ground; get your guests out
Once a buffalo charge begins it is rarely a mock charge, so get your guests out of there.
What is the gestation period of a buffalo?
Most mating is in February and a single calf is born after 11 months.
Old buffalo bulls that stay together
Dominant bulls in the breeding herd
Old bulls, or "dagga boys", tend to stay with other old bulls.
How can the age of a buffalo be estimated?
By horn growth and how sparse the coat is
By counting rings on the hooves
By the colour of the eyes
By the length of the tail
Horns keep growing and the coat becomes sparser with age, so these features can be used to estimate age.
What is a lion's best sense?
A lion's best sense is its sight and it will immediately stare at any disturbance.
Which are early warning signs from a lion?
Body flattened, ears back and tail flicking
Early warning signs include flattening the body in a crouch, ears back and tail flicking.
On foot, a lion becomes aware of you. What should you do first?
Stand your ground and let the lion react
Point it out to the guests
Do not move away immediately; stand your ground and allow the lion to react.
When should you retreat during a lion encounter on foot?
After the lion's reaction is over and it has settled
As soon as you see the lion
When the lion turns its back on you
Wait until the lion's initial reaction is over and it has settled down before retreating.
What is the gestation period of a lion?
Lionesses usually have 2-3 cubs after a gestation of 3,5 months.
At what age are male lions evicted from the pride?
Males are evicted from the pride between 2-4 years of age.
Why do male lions often form coalitions?
Two medium-strength males can beat one strong male
It stops cubs being killed by hyaena
Two medium-strength lions can often defeat one very powerful and experienced lion.
Which statement about lion vocalisation is correct?
The roar is heard up to 1km away
The roar is over 110 decibels and heard from at least 5km; lions grunt, growl and snarl but cannot purr.
You are on foot and close to a leopard that your guests have not seen. What should you do?
Do not point it out and quietly leave
Point it out so guests can watch
Walk closer for a better view
Stare at it to keep it calm
If guests may not spot it, do not point it out; a leopard that feels unseen will not react aggressively.
If a leopard charges, what does the manual advise?
Stand still and avoid direct eye contact
If a charge results, stand still and avoid direct eye contact until it is over, then continue retreating.
How should you retreat from a leopard giving warning signs?
Back off, preferably at an angle
Turn and run in a straight line
Immediately begin backing off, preferably at an angle (diagonally away from the cat).
How long are a leopard cub's eyes closed after birth?
Cubs weigh about 300-500g at birth and their eyes are closed for the first 10 days.
Leopard territorial calling is described as sounding like what?
Someone cutting wood with a rough saw
Leopard vocalise with a harsh rasping sound like someone cutting wood with a rough saw.
What top speed can a cheetah reach?
Cheetah reach over 100km/hr and accelerate from 0-100km/hr in 3 seconds.
How does a cheetah usually react to people on foot if it has an escape route?
Unless cornered, a cheetah will never attack a human and will run if it has an escape route.
What is the gestation period of a cheetah?
A litter of about 4 kittens is born after 3 months, weighing about 250g.
Which call is typical of the cheetah?
Cheetah make a bird-like chirp heard for several hundred metres.
What is the hunting style of the wild dog called?
Wild dog hunting is called coursing: they walk towards prey and run it down when it flees.
What is the average wild dog pack size in Botswana?
Wild dog are gregarious and pack size in Botswana is on average 8-10.
Which statement about wild dog and people on foot is correct?
They always flee and pose no threat
They attack if you stand still
Wild dog will always flee from humans and pose no threat to people on foot.
When do wild dogs breed in Botswana?
In Botswana wild dog breed in winter, mating around April and denning around June.
On average, how many pups does a wild dog female give birth to?
After a gestation of 2,5 months the female gives birth to an average of 10 pups.
Which wild dog call is used to regroup after a hunt?
The loud HOOO HOOO call is given when trying to regroup after a hunt.
When is the peak breeding time for spotted hyaena?
Hyaena breed all year but peak in December/January when young antelope are abundant.
What colour are spotted hyaena cubs?
Cubs are black; spotting begins to emerge on the flanks by 4 months.
Spotted hyaena use 'pasting' to mark territory. What is pasted, and where?
Anal pouch scent on grass stems
Pasting is done on grass stems using the anal pouch.
Which statement about brown hyaena is correct?
They are totally independent of surface water
They hunt more than they scavenge
They live in a matriarchal clan
They are active mainly by day
Brown hyaena are totally independent of surface water and are nocturnal scavengers that seldom hunt.
Why does brown hyaena breeding suit the Kalahari's harshest time?
Many animals die then, giving plenty of food
There is more water at that time
Grass is greenest at that time
Births coincide with the harshest time, when many animals die, providing plentiful food for scavengers.
With whom do brown hyaena females frequently breed?
Breeding is frequently not with males of the clan but with nomadic males.
According to the large herbivore table, what does a male giraffe weigh on average?
The table gives giraffe males 1200kg and females 820kg.
What is the gestation period of a giraffe?
A single giraffe calf is born after a 15 month gestation, with a birth drop of about 2 metres.
Why is a young giraffe moved after almost every feed?
So the scent of lactation does not attract predators
So it can find better browse
So the herd can find it
The calf is moved so that the scent of lactation does not linger and attract predators.
How do male giraffe change with age?
They become darker and develop lumps on the head
They become paler and lose their ossicones
Their spots become larger and rounder
Males become darker with age and develop lumps on the head from calcium deposits.
When fleeing from predators, where does the zebra stallion position himself?
At the back, between the group and the predator
At the front, leading the group
In the middle, among the foals
The stallion drops to the back and stays between the group and the predator, kicking out.
How does a young zebra stallion start his own harem?
He steals a filly on heat from another herd
He fights the old stallion to the death
He waits for his mother's herd
Mares choose him at a lek
A stallion ready to compete steals a filly on heat from another male's herd.
What percentage of zebra oestrus happens in summer?
Mares come into oestrus all year but 80% of the time it happens in summer.
What is the typical call of the plains zebra?
Zebra give the typical call "HWO-HWHOOOP" repeated several times, and a horse-like snort.
How often must blue wildebeest drink?
Blue wildebeest are water dependent and must drink at least every second day.
What is a 'pulse-birth', as seen in wildebeest?
All calves are born in a very short space of time
Calves are born at night only
In a pulse-birth all calves are born in a short time so predators cannot eat them all.
What is the gestation period of the blue wildebeest?
Mating is in March/April and a calf is born in November/December after 8,5 months.
What is the wildebeest's only defence against lions?
Wildebeest can defend against smaller predators in a group, but speed (up to 80km/hr) is their only defence against lions.
How does a lone oryx defend itself?
Backs into a thorn-bush and lowers its horns
When alone, oryx reverse into a thorn-bush and lower the head, facing horns at the attacker.
What do oryx often dig for?
Oryx are ruminant grazers but frequently dig for bulbs and tubers and occasionally browse.
What is the main defence of waterbuck when attacked?
Their main defence is running through water; males also use their horns.
What does the manual say about the idea that waterbuck smell makes their meat distasteful?
There is no evidence to support it
There is no evidence for this, and waterbuck are often victims of predation.
In large, highly mobile herds, what breeding system do red lechwe males use?
In small sedentary herds males are territorial, but in large mobile herds males use a lek.
When is the peak breeding season for red lechwe in the Okavango?
Peak breeding is January/February in Linyanti and March/April in the Okavango.
Up to how many times a day do red lechwe drink?
Lechwe are water dependent and drink up to 3 times a day.
Up to what percentage of kudu browsing may be done at night?
Kudu are mainly diurnal browsers but up to 40% of browsing may be done at night.
How are most disputes between kudu bulls settled?
Fighting between kudu bulls is rare and most disputes over cows are settled by posturing.
By what age have a kudu bull's horns reached about 2½ turns?
The horn completes its first spiral at 2 years and has 2½ turns by 6.
What does the kudu alarm call sound like?
The kudu alarm bark is loud and almost baboon-like.
Impala are described as 'intermediate feeders'. What does this mean?
They prefer fresh grass but switch to browse
They eat both meat and plants
Impala prefer grass when fresh and switch to browse when crude protein in the grass gets low.
Why are a herd's impala ewes covered by 3 or 4 strong males during the rut?
One ram cannot keep up the effort for 3 weeks
A ram cannot sustain the energy needed for the full 3 week rut, so the 3 or 4 strongest males cover the ewes.
When are impala fawns dropped in a pulse-birth?
Impala fawns are dropped in a pulse-birth in November.
What method of hunting does the caracal use?
Caracal are solitary, mainly nocturnal predators with a stalk and pounce method of hunting.
What is the gestation period of a caracal?
After a gestation of 80 days an average of 2 cubs are born.
What are the serval's massive ears adapted for?
Hunting in long grass and swamps
The massive ears are adapted for hunting in long grass and swampy habitats where visibility is poor.
What is the gestation period of a serval?
Peak breeding is in late summer, when 2-3 kittens are born after a gestation of 70 days.
What is a major threat to the African wildcat?
Genetic pollution through inter-breeding with feral cats is a major threat.
What is the first sign that an African wildcat population has been affected by inter-breeding?
Loss of the reddish colour behind the ears
Loss of spots on the legs
The first sign is when they lose the reddish colour behind the ears.
Where are African wildcat kittens usually born?
In disused springhare or aardvark burrows
An average of 3 kittens are usually born in disused springhare or aardvark burrows.
What do spotted-necked otters mainly feed on?
Spotted-necked otter are aquatic predators feeding mainly on small fish and crabs.
Under which CITES appendix is the spotted-necked otter protected?
The spotted-necked otter is protected under CITES Appendix 2.
What does the black and white colouring of the honey badger signal?
A warning not to attack it (aposematic)
The black and white colouring is aposematic - a warning to other animals not to engage.
How does loose skin help a honey badger in a fight?
It can turn and bite an attacker holding its neck
It lets it squeeze into burrows
The loose skin lets the badger turn in its skin and bite the face and neck of the attacker.
What does the honey badger use as a secondary defence?
A pair of anal pouches release a very unpleasant-smelling fluid used as a secondary defence.
In pairs that share a territory
Jackals live in pairs and share a territory, chasing other jackal away.
How long does a black-backed jackal live in the wild?
Jackal pups disperse before one year old and live to about 6 years in the wild.
What is special about the bat-eared fox's diet?
It is the only mainly insectivorous canid
Bat-eared fox are the only primarily insectivorous canid.
How many teeth can a bat-eared fox have?
The bat-eared fox can have in excess of 50 teeth, more than any other African land mammal.
When is the bat-eared fox mostly active?
By day in winter and by night in summer
They are predominantly diurnal in winter and nocturnal in summer.
Why is the slender mongoose often mobbed by starlings and other birds?
It climbs trees to forage for nesting birds
It steals food from bird feeders
It is the best climber of the mongooses and forages in trees for nesting birds.
Where do groups of dwarf mongoose usually live?
Dwarf mongoose groups usually live in disused termite mounds.
In dwarf mongoose groups, what is 'allo parenting'?
Group members other than the parents baby-sit the young
Young being raised by another species
Often it is not the parents that baby-sit the young while the group forages - this is allo parenting.
What is the maximum group size given for dwarf mongoose?
Dwarf mongoose are social and live in groups of up to 30 members.
Hares re-eat soft green pellets to help digest grass. What is this called?
Re-eating soft pellets is called coprophagy; it lets hares extract elements such as vitamin B.
When is the peak breeding season of the savanna (scrub) hare?
Peak breeding is December to March and an average of 2 young are born.
Vervet monkeys have different alarm calls for different threats. Which three does the manual list?
Terrestrial predator, bird of prey and python
Vervets give different alarm calls for a terrestrial predator, a bird of prey or a python.
What is the gestation period of a vervet monkey?
Vervets have a single young at any time of year after about 160 days.
In vervet and baboon troops, which animals stay in their troop of birth?
Troops are female-bonded; males disperse from troop to troop and females stay in their birth troop.
When a chacma baboon troop is feeding, where do dominant males tend to move?
Near the front of the troop
In the middle of the troop
At the back of the troop
Dominant males move near the front, dominant females in the middle and low-ranking males at the back.
What is the gestation period of the chacma baboon?
Baboon gestation is 6 months and a single young is born; breeding is all year.
